newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RANGERS TRADE KEN HILL TO ANGELS FOR JIM LEYRITZ.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RANGERS TRADE KEN HILL TO ANGELS FOR JIM LEYRITZ.

text.p: The Texas Rangers traded pitcher Ken Hill, who has only one win in his last seven starts, to the Anaheim Angels Tuesday for catcher Jim Leyritz and a player to be named.

Hill, who last season went 16-10 with a 3.63 earned run average over 250 innings to anchor the Rangers' starting rotation, has failed to find that form this year, going 5-8 with a 5.19 ERA in 19 starts.
He has surrendered 129 hits over 111 innings and has been shelled for 22 runs and 29 hits over 20 1/3 innings in his last four starts.

The 33-year-old Leyritz, well-known for his post-season heroics as a member of the New York Yankees' 1996 championship team, hit .276 (81-for-294) with 11 homers and 50 runs batted in for the Angels this season. Leyritz, in his seventh season overall, is batting .268 with 68 homers and 293 RBI.
The acquisition of Leyritz also increases the possiblity the Rangers may move catcher Ivan Rodriguez before Thursday's trading deadline.

The 25-year-old Rodriguez, who is hitting .334 with 11 homers and 47 RBI this season, turned down a five-year, $38 million guaranteed contract last week from Rangers owner J. Thomas Schieffer. Schieffer tried to further sweeten the deal by adding two option years at $8 million per year, to no avail.

The 31-year-old Hill, a three-time 16-game winner, will be joining his fifth team in his 10-year major-league career. In his years with the Cardinals, Expos, Indians and Rangers, Hill has posted a lifetime mark of 95-79 with a 3.77 ERA in 252 starts.

Hill's .614 winning percentage entering this season ranked him eighth among active major-league starters coming into this season. In post-season play, he is a combined 2-1 with both Texas and Cleveland. His only loss came with the Indians in the 1995 World Series.
The versatile Leyritz has started at catcher, first base, third base and designated hitter in his major-league career. As a Yankee in 1994, he established career highs of 17 homers and 58 RBI.
The Rangers were in Baltimore Tuesday night to play the Orioles.
